claim: Did you know… parachutes do not prevent death when jumping from aircraft?

studies.finding: A randomized trial found no deaths or major injuries in either parachute or empty-backpack jumpers leaving an aircraft.
studies.verdict: Real result, but the planes were parked, 0.6 metres up.

claim: Did you know… high-risk heart failure patients do better when cardiologists are away?

studies.cite: Jena et al. (2015), JAMA Internal Medicine
studies.finding: Thirty-day mortality for high-risk heart failure and cardiac arrest was lower on dates of national cardiology meetings, in teaching hospitals.
studies.verdict: Single observational study; benefit limited to teaching hospitals.

claim: Did you know… left-handed people die years earlier than right-handed people?

studies.cite: Halpern & Coren (1991), New England Journal of Medicine
studies.finding: A letter reported that left-handers in a sample of deaths had died markedly younger than right-handers.
studies.verdict: Published as a short letter reporting a survival disadvantage.

studies.finding: A long commentary reviewed the early-death argument and found the evidence could not sustain it.
studies.verdict: Conclusion: the decreased-survival hypothesis does not hold up.

studies.cite: Aggleton et al. (1993), Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health
studies.finding: Among deceased first-class cricketers, left-handers lived about 25 months less, partly through more accidental and war deaths.
studies.verdict: A small gap, much of it from accidents and war.

claim: Did you know… fake knee surgery relieved arthritis pain as well as real surgery?

studies.cite: Moseley et al. (2002), New England Journal of Medicine
studies.finding: In 180 patients, arthroscopic lavage and debridement did no better than a placebo operation.
studies.verdict: Confidence intervals excluded any clinically meaningful difference from placebo.

claim: Did you know… a doctor cracked one hand's knuckles for fifty years as an experiment?

studies.finding: A physician cracked the knuckles of his left hand for about fifty years and left his right hand alone; neither developed arthritis.
studies.verdict: A single-person letter, not a proof on its own.

studies.cite: deWeber et al. (2011), Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine
studies.finding: In 215 people, hand osteoarthritis appeared in 18.1% of habitual knuckle crackers and 21.5% of non-crackers.
studies.verdict: Case-control study agrees: no link between cracking and hand osteoarthritis.

claim: Did you know… patients operated on by their surgeon on the surgeon's birthday die more often?

studies.finding: Among Medicare patients over 65, 30-day mortality after emergency surgery was 6.9% on the surgeon's birthday versus 5.6% on other days.
studies.verdict: Observational, only 2,064 birthday cases; the authors could not identify a mechanism.

claim: Did you know… the Monday after clocks spring forward brings 24% more heart attacks?

studies.finding: In Michigan, angioplasty-treated heart attacks rose 24% the Monday after the spring change and fell 21% the Tuesday after the fall change.
studies.verdict: Authors saw shifted timing, not higher totals, with no correction for multiple comparisons.

claim: Did you know… most statin side effects also occur when patients take a placebo?

studies.cite: Wood et al. (2020), New England Journal of Medicine
studies.finding: Patients who had quit statins over side effects scored similar symptoms on atorvastatin (16.3) and placebo (15.4) in a 12-month n-of-1 trial.
studies.verdict: Small trial; about 90% of the symptom burden also came with placebo.
